meta.title: EKD devices | OpenAmpere
meta.description: Which batteries, wallboxes and other devices EKD sold, and which of them OpenAmpere can monitor and control.

head.title: Which EKD devices work with OpenAmpere?
head.lead: Since 2018, EKD has sold batteries, wallboxes and other devices of several makers. This page shows what OpenAmpere can do with them today and what is being worked on.
head.find: Which device you have is on the type plate of the battery, the inverter or the wallbox. The sales name is usually in EKD's offer or invoice.

next.tellUs: Get in touch if you have one

rows.e3Note: Confirmed on an H3 with newer firmware, the 22 kW model not yet.
rows.e2Note: In daily use on an owner's system; the control functions not yet checked one by one.
rows.solarmaxNote: Monitoring first. OpenAmpere never switches on a battery that EKD switched off remotely.
rows.enphaseNote: Monitoring first. Needs a key from the Enphase account once.
rows.senecNote: Possibly also older Senec.Home V2.1. Senec has no Modbus TCP interface, so it needs a new kind of connection.
rows.vartaNote: Unclear how many there are and which interface they have.
rows.chargeProNote: Controls only after you switch it on for the wallbox in the app.
rows.chargeNote: evcc needs a sponsor token for it. Directly through OpenAmpere is planned.
rows.iqNote: OpenAmpere replaces the app. You can take over the history from the EKD cloud while it runs.
rows.heaterNote: Not yet confirmed on a real system.
rows.heatpumpNote: Through a Shelly relay on the SG Ready input, not yet confirmed.

notes.planned: Every planned device has an issue on GitHub, but no date yet. Monitoring comes first. Control comes only after an owner has confirmed the values on their system.
notes.testers: Do you have such a device and can test? Then please say so in the issue: which device according to the type plate. Leave out the serial number, because the issue is public.
notes.sources: Details and sources for every device are in the device overview in the repository.
